summary.root_cause_text: Ops config change set queue_max 1000 -> 0, so every new order was rejected with 'queue full, message dropped' while the API still returned 200.
recommended: Have a human contact the customers or re-submit the dropped orders (about ids 15-34), since reprocess_orders only covers processed orders that have no payment.
Add validation so queue_max cannot be set to 0.

events.text:
version: v1.3
payment_provider_url: internal://payments-v1
queue_max: 0
worker_count: 1
sync_interval_s: 5
queue_max: 0 -> 1000. Confirmed: the service is now using the new value.
All business invariants green (health, payments, queue, worker, ledger, errors, latency).

Since those dropped orders live only in the in-memory queue, they're unrecoverable once lost — I can't reprocess them automatically. Best to escalate and recommend human re-submission for those cases, then submit.

root_causes: Ops config change set queue_max 1000 -> 0, so every new order was rejected with 'queue full, message dropped' while the API still returned 200.

money_impact queued_orders: count 20, SAR 2854.8, USD 1790.12, total_sar 9567.75
args.impact: At least 20 orders were accepted by the API but dropped and never paid. The count was still rising when I checked, 12 in the alert and 20 by the latest read. money_impact: SAR 2854.8 plus USD 1790.12, total_sar 9567.75. The dropped orders were in the in-memory queue and are not reprocessable with the tools I have.
recommended_actions: Have a human contact the customers or re-submit the dropped orders (about ids 15-34), since reprocess_orders only covers processed orders that have no payment.
Add validation so queue_max cannot be set to 0.
args.summary: An ops config change set queue_max to 0, and the queue silently dropped every new order while /health stayed green. I restored queue_max to 1000 and the invariants are green. The roughly 20 orders dropped before the fix are not recoverable with the tools I have and need manual re-submission."
